title: What is the balance when a credit follows a negative balance?
description: A bank account owes twenty rupees, and a credit of two hundred rupees comes in the next day. The credit first pays off the twenty owed, and the rest is the new balance. Keeko adds the twenty by mistake.
teaching_notes: One idea: a credit first fills the gap below zero, and what is left is the new balance. Watch for students who add the amount owed to the credit.

source: Your strategic large purchase the previous day allows you to make ₹200 at your business the next day. What is your balance now?
video_script.why: The child adds a credit to a negative balance and sees the credit pay off what is owed first.
video_script.substitution: Use the credit to pay off the amount owed first; what is left of the credit is the new balance.
video_script.wrong_move: adds the twenty rupees owed to the credit, as if the twenty had been saved in the account
video_script.payoff_line: The balance is now one hundred and eighty rupees.
maths_rules: the balance starts at −₹20, so ₹20 is owed
a credit of ₹200 is money put in: +200
the first ₹20 of the credit pays off what is owed
video_script.design: One idea: a credit first fills the gap below the empty line, and what is left is the new balance. The first twenty rupees of the credit drop into the gap. Keeko adds the twenty owed to the credit, and the gap shows the slip.
